title: Finite-type torsion morphisms satisfy the universal nearby-cycle finiteness condition
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\geq1$, and let $g:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a geometric point $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], write $X_{(x)}$ and $Y_{(g(x))}$ for the strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $g_{(x)}:X_{(x)}\to Y_{(g(x))}$ for the induced morphism. Direct images are on the small etale module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $g$ satisfies condition (*) universally, meaning the following precise assertion: for every base change $g':X'=X\times_YY'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], there is an open covering $X'=\bigcup_\alpha U_\alpha$ and integers $N_\alpha\geq0$ such that for every geometric point $x'$ of $U_\alpha$, every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X'_{(x')}$, and every $q>N_\alpha$, one has $R^qg'_{(x')*}F=0$.

source.place: Definition A.1 and the sentence before Remark A.2, p. 1 (Gabber finiteness, cited there as [O, Proposition 3.1] and [I, Corollary 1.15]); local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary morphism $Y'\to Y$ and put $g':X'=X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], $g'$ is locally of finite type; this statement imposes no quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis on $Y'$. For each point of $X'$ choose an affine open $V\subset Y'$ containing its image and an affine open $U\subset g'^{-1}(V)$ containing the point. Such $U$ form an open covering of $X'$. The restriction $h:U\to V$ is locally of finite type: every affine pair in $U,V$ is an affine pair in $X',Y'$, so apply both directions of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs].

The map $h:U\to V$ between affine schemes is quasi-compact. Explicitly write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The inverse image of a distinguished open $D(a)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B_{h^\#(a)}$; every affine open of $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence has a finite distinguished-open cover, whose inverse images are again quasi-compact by the same node. A finite union of quasi-compact spaces is quasi-compact, proving the assertion. Thus $h$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Also $V$ is quasi-compact by the affine-scheme node. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to obtain $d_U\ge0$ with every fibre of $h$ of dimension at most $d_U$. The bound is allowed to depend on the chart.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0A3V (lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension); elementary distinguished-open calculation for quasi-compactness

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $x'$ of $U$ and let $y'=g'(x')\in V$. The strict localizations $U_{(x')}$ and $X'_{(x')}$ are canonically the same, and likewise $V_{(y')}$ and $Y'_{(y')}$. To check this directly from [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], a pointed etale neighbourhood of $x'$ in $X'$ can be restricted to its inverse image of $U$ and then to an affine open containing its distinguished point. This is a pointed etale neighbourhood in $U$ mapping to the original neighbourhood. These neighbourhoods form a full subcategory of the affine pointed neighbourhoods in the defining colimit. That indexing category is cofiltered as stated in the strict-localization definition. The preceding refinement verifies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1), so its colimit is unchanged. The identical argument applies to $V\subset Y'$. The induced morphisms agree: compatibility with these neighbourhood maps is clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], so under these identifications $h_{(x')}=g'_{(x')}$.

source.place: Strict-localization definition; restriction to an open neighbourhood and functoriality

proof.text: The equation $m\Lambda=0$ makes $\Lambda$ a $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-algebra: the unit map $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ factors through the quotient, since multiples of $m$ map to zero. For the fixed chart $h$ in step 2, [lem-trf-gabber-strict-local-torsion-bound] now applies with $N=d_U$. It gives $R^q h_{(x')*}F=0$ for every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{(x')}$ and every $q>2d_U$, as a sheaf on $V_{(y')}$. By step 3 this is exactly $R^q g'_{(x')*}F=0$ on $Y'_{(y')}$ for every $F$ on $X'_{(x')}$.

source.place: Illusie Corollary 1.15, under Theorem 1.14; Zheng sentence preceding Remark A.2

proof.text: Set $N_U=2d_U\ge0$ for each chart of the open cover chosen in step 1. Step 4 proves the required vanishing uniformly for all geometric points of that chart, all sheaves and all $q>N_U$. This is exactly condition (*) as expanded in the statement. The morphism $Y'\to Y$ was arbitrary, so the assertion holds universally. If $X'$ is empty the empty covering satisfies the assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q33-e2c675dbc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Neither source is in the local literature mirror (WANTED is correct), so I read both online. Zheng's Künneth appendix, Def. A.1 and the next sentence: a torsion Λ (equivalent to mΛ=0) and f locally of finite type give condition (*) universally; the item states this exactly, with the same Λ-module coefficient category on strict localizations. Illusie, Around Thom–Sebastiani, Cor. 1.15 (pp. 15–16), with the hypotheses of Thm 1.14 (Gabber/Orgogozo 3.1): no noetherian or invertibility hypothesis; the new node lem-trf-gabber-strict-local-torsion-bound states the same hypotheses and conclusion (Z/mZ-algebra, locally of finite type, fibre dimension ≤ N, any geometric point and any Λ-sheaf G, R^q f_(x)* G = 0 for q > 2N) and is statement-only. Step 1 uses the base-change and affine-pair Mathlib leaves with no hypothesis on Y'. Step 2 checks quasi-compactness of the affine chart through distinguished opens and applies the fibre-bound node, whose hypotheses (finite type, quasi-compact target) hold. Step 3: neighbourhoods in U form a full subcategory because U→X' is a monomorphism, refinement gives the hypothesis of colimit-initial (1), and clause (4) of functoriality (or uniqueness in (3)) gives equality of the induced maps. Step 4 checks the coefficient factorisation and applies the new node with N=d_U. Step 5 closes the quantifiers with N_U=2d_U and the empty cover. The new node is strictly smaller than the item (fixed morphism, global bound; it is the source's own named input). rg over the DAG and a blueprint grep found no duplicate. Small cases checked: identity with N=0, A^1 over an algebraically closed field, p-torsion Λ over Z, m=1, empty fibres. I accept both declared tool uses (fibre-dimension bound, strict-henselization functoriality) as generic black boxes. No fixes.
